title: Manila: the promoter's cars and the weak musicians
summary: In Manila the promoter provided each member's make of car, and the local musicians were poor compared with Japan.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: On the trip to the Orient, we came back through -- we came to Manila and we played a large stadium in Manila; the man that owns it and the promoter, his name was, let's see, Arnetta -- he was supposed to be the wealthiest man in Manila. Now when he brings an act in, he finds out what type of automobile everybody in the group drives, and that's your car when you're in Manila. They meet you at the airport, you know, and if you drive a Chrysler, there's a Chrysler there for you. I was a Mercedes man, and there was a Mercedes there for me, and right on down the line.

But he had 39 automobiles. 39 automobiles. But he had this palatial mansion, and he had a couple of -- they weren't kids, they were adults -- but one was going to Georgetown University, and both of them played golf, so you know, I was right at home. We played that country club over there quite a bit, but ...

Manila was a little different, I think, than other places we had been because their musicians were not almost up to it, you know? They had bad musicians. They couldn't play very well at all. After coming from Japan, where the musicians were great -- the band that traveled with us over there had the name of Sharps and Flats -- so that shows you where they were. That was the name of the band that toured with us. But we went to Nagoya and I think about 5 cities in all.
